description: The 8 canonical research questions for the Zepto AI Review Engine. These questions drive the relevance filter keyword list (Phase 2), the semantic retrieval queries (Phase 5), and the structure of the final report (Phase 7). Do not change these without assessing the downstream impact on the preprocessed corpus.

questions.label: Habit & Repetition
questions.question: Why do users repeatedly buy from the same categories? Is it convenience, trust, or lack of awareness?
questions.semantic_query: I always buy the same things every week and never try anything new from this app. I just stick to what I know.

metadata_filters.note: No source or rating filter — applies broadly across all users.

questions.label: Exploration Barriers
questions.question: What prevents users from trying new categories? (e.g., price anxiety, unfamiliarity, no trigger)
questions.semantic_query: I wanted to try the pet food or beauty section but I was not sure about the quality or price. Ended up not buying.

metadata_filters.note: Prefer 1–3 star reviews for stronger signal on barriers and frustrations.

questions.label: Discovery Pathways
questions.question: How do users currently discover products or categories they were not already buying?
questions.semantic_query: I discovered a new product because of a recommendation or offer and it became something I buy regularly now.

metadata_filters.note: 4–5 star reviews more likely to contain positive discovery moments.

questions.label: Role of Habit
questions.question: How strongly do established routines suppress willingness to experiment with new categories?
questions.semantic_query: I have a fixed list I order every time. I don't really look at other sections because my list is already set.

metadata_filters.note: No filter. Look for mentions of fixed shopping lists, schedules, or auto-reorder behavior.

questions.label: Information Needs
questions.question: What information do users need before they feel confident trying a new category for the first time?
questions.semantic_query: I would try the medicine or baby products section if I knew more about the brands or if there were reviews I could trust.

metadata_filters.note: No source filter. Look for qualifiers, conditions, and 'I wish' statements.

questions.label: Recurring Frustrations
questions.question: What pain points surface consistently across reviews and discussions? How do these suppress exploration?
questions.semantic_query: The app is frustrating because I can never find what I am looking for. The search is bad and categories are confusing.

metadata_filters.note: Filter to 1–3 star reviews for the strongest frustration signal.

questions.label: Experimental Segments
questions.question: Which user personas or life-stage segments are more likely to try new categories?
questions.semantic_query: Since we had a baby I started buying so many new things from the app. Or since I got a dog I started exploring the pet section.

metadata_filters.note: Look for life-event triggers: new baby, new pet, moving house, health goal, new city.

questions.label: Unmet Needs
questions.question: What needs do users consistently express that the platform is not currently addressing?
questions.semantic_query: I wish Zepto had better options for organic food or more variety in the premium section. There are things I would buy if they were available.

metadata_filters.note: Look for 'I wish', 'why don't they have', 'missing', 'should add', 'no option for'.

derived_artifacts.relevance_filter_keywords: Union of all relevance_keywords arrays across all 8 questions. Used in Phase 2 preprocessing to determine which records to retain.
derived_artifacts.semantic_queries: The semantic_query field for each question is the actual string submitted to the vector DB in Phase 5, NOT the human-readable question field.
derived_artifacts.metadata_filters: Applied at retrieval time in Phase 5 to sharpen evidence for specific questions. Not applied globally.
